Technical review distinguishes count, polymer mass, specificity, sensitivity, throughput and cost. Background and retained size fractions limit cross-study comparisons. No universal instrument or health conclusion.

Implementation feasibility examples are not universal validation. Collection vs blank filters, matrix overload and transfer losses preserved. Surfacewater adaptation conditional; mass and counts not interchangeable.

Workshop critical appraisal prioritizes oral mammalian in vivo evidence; no reliable heterogeneous environmental human threshold. Conservative screening level nonregulatory, not demonstrated human safety cutoff. No claim comprehensive search.

2016 dated statement: preparation may degrade plastic; enumeration and chemical identification separate; air/equipment QA and incompatible seafood units matter. Occurrence, food processing, toxicokinetic and toxicity gaps retained without claims about later evidence or current law.

Dated decision adopts drinking-water Annex and addresses Member States. IR/Raman particle identification vs thermal mass; collection/blank/recovery distinctions and reference-spectrum/size/shape/reporting requirements directly supported. No health ceiling or product concentration finding.

Water-contact extraction differs for nylon; glass controls alongside. Pixel count explicitly considered microplastic count: not discrete object reconstruction. Visual counts and representative Raman-confirmed subset yield estimate, not every-object confirmation. Below-validated-size extraction, lab-specific MDA, trained analysts and air/field/reagent/fortified blank distinctions preserved. No safety concentration.
